headline: High: LightAgent’s broad tool/network surface can amplify Copilot outputs into unsafe actions, while shared-file and prompt-injection risks remain plausible but not directly evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads editor buffers and repo context, while LightAgent can use MCP and tool calls with runtime hooks. If Copilot-generated or user-supplied content is passed into LightAgent prompts or tools, instruction-like text could steer actions. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF Copilot output is copied into LightAgent prompts or MCP inputs, prompt injection becomes actionable.
IF LightAgent runtime hooks forward untrusted content into tool calls, attacker instructions can persist.
mitigations: Keep Copilot output out of LightAgent system/tool prompts.
Add a manual review step before any LightAgent tool call using Copilot-generated text.
Strip instructions from copied code/comments before reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, and LightAgent handles conversations, memory, tool results, and secrets such as API keys. A shared workspace or copied context could move sensitive code into LightAgent’s broader egress surface. No direct shared filesystem is documented, so the risk is inferred and not proven.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or copied buffers, sensitive code can flow into LightAgent memory.
IF LightAgent sends tool results or memory to external APIs, leaked content can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in files visible to Copilot.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Redact API keys before any LightAgent interaction.
Review LightAgent memory and trace retention settings.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries at the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while LightAgent can spawn subprocesses, use MCP, and has broad network egress. If both operate on the same repo or mutable resource, concurrent edits or conflicting tool actions are plausible. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository concurrently, file and git conflicts can occur.
IF LightAgent MCP tools mutate shared state while Copilot proposes edits, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time on a repo.
Use separate branches for each agent.
Require human approval before git commits.
Disable LightAgent write-capable tools for shared projects.
requires-engineering: add workspace locks and conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces edits and chat suggestions from repo context, and LightAgent can act on tool calls, browser actions, and subprocesses. If LightAgent treats Copilot output as authoritative, a mistaken suggestion can cascade into external actions or workflow state changes. Because LightAgent has action authority and no verification step is documented, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF LightAgent consumes Copilot output without independent verification, errors can propagate into tool actions.
IF Copilot suggests an incorrect fix that LightAgent executes, downstream state may be altered.
mitigations: Require LightAgent to verify Copilot outputs against source files.
Block direct execution of Copilot-generated commands.
Use a second human review for any browser or subprocess action.
Log provenance for every instruction passed between agents.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks before actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source GitHub/Microsoft service with vendor-only egress and GitHub repo OAuth context, while LightAgent is open-source but handles API keys, memory, and broad egress. If regulated or sensitive data is present, the pair can create residency and retention mismatches. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into both agents, retention and residency obligations must be checked.
IF LightAgent stores traces or memory longer than Copilot context, deletion/export obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Confirm retention settings for LightAgent traces and memory.
Review GitHub Copilot data handling terms before use.
Separate projects by data classification.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing and deletion.
